brief: Goldman's January forecast expected core PCE at 2.3% by August; it printed 3.0%. Goldman's post-mortem attributes about half the 0.7pp overshoot to AI-exposed consumer electronics and software, though it argues software is overweighted and not quality-adjusted in PCE, inflating the measured effect; the bank still expects three-fourths of the surprise to fade, forecasting core PCE at 2.2% by December 2027. Meanwhile the Fed's September minutes show all 19 officials backing a hike to 3.75%-4.00%, with most expecting another by year-end, explicitly citing the AI buildout as an inflation driver for the first time. Fed officials (Daly, Schmid, Musalem, Goolsbee) argue relief is distant because hyperscaler capex is rate-insensitive, citing continued double-digit capex growth that keeps the memory and chip shortage running into 2028-2030. The pressure is spreading internationally (BoJ, Temasek), with Temasek naming an AI-trade unwind its top 2027 risk. The piece frames resolution as either hyperscalers slowing spend or the Fed hiking until something breaks, noting a brief Nasdaq selloff on an OpenAI revenue miss before stocks recovered to new highs.
